mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLS 220/250 CDI OM651 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the OM651 is fundamentally a reliable engine, with many examples exceeding 200,000-300,000 km [10†L8]. However, it has predictable weak points: timing chain stretch and guide wear from approximately 120,000 km [10†L39], EGR valve clogging, swirl flap failure, and injector seal leaks ("Black Death") [6†L4-L8]. OM651 is robust and capable of high mileage with proper maintenance. Timing chain rattle on cold start is the early warning sign [9†L15-L18]. Regular oil and filter changes every 10,000 miles are critical for longevity. A 2015 recall addressed timing chain tensioner seal ring oil leaks [8†L19-L25].

mainEntity.name: What is the "Black Death" problem on the Mercedes CLS 220/250 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: "Black Death" is the common term for injector seal failure on Mercedes diesel engines [6†L28-L31]. When the seals fail, unburnt diesel and exhaust gases escape, creating a hard, tar-like carbon buildup around the injector seats [6†L4-L8]. Symptoms: chuffing noise from engine bay, black residue around injectors, fuel odour [6†L48-L49][6†L37-L39]. If ignored, injectors can seize and cylinder head damage can occur. Specialist seal replacement costs £300-£500. Catch it early - the repair is far cheaper than engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes CLS 220/250 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Well-maintained OM651 engines regularly exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. With meticulous maintenance, some have reached 300,000 miles without major failures [10†L8]. OM651: 150k-200k+ miles with regular servicing. Timing chain stretch typically occurs from 75,000-120,000 miles [10†L39]. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles significantly extends life.

These engines made the CLS accessible to a broader audience, combining the four-door coupé's style with impressive fuel economy and lower running costs.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLS 220/250 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The OM651 2.1-litre diesel in the CLS 220 BlueTEC and CLS 250 CDI is fundamentally robust, with many examples exceeding 200,000-300,000 km. However, like any diesel of its era, it has predictable weak points: timing chain stretch and guide wear at higher mileages, EGR valve clogging, swirl flap mechanism failure in the intake manifold, and injector seal leaks (the classic "Black Death"). Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Wear - The OM651's Critical Weakness
problems.rootCause: The OM651 uses a simplex timing chain installed on the transmission side of the engine. The chain can stretch over time, and the tensioner can fail, causing a rattling noise on cold start. In 2015, Mercedes issued a recall for a timing chain tensioner seal ring that could leak oil. If the chain stretches beyond tolerance or a guide fails, the consequences range from misfires and cam/crank correlation codes to catastrophic engine damage if the chain jumps a tooth.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; tensioner wear only

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Full Timing Chain & Sprocket Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets. Transmission removal required due to rear-mounted chain
Supply & fit fully rebuilt OM651 engine with new timing components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped and valves have contacted pistons

problems.recommendation: Rattling on cold start for 1-3 seconds is the early warning sign of timing chain tensioner failure. Don't ignore it - a Mercedes technician advised getting the chain, guides and sprockets done at ~90,000 miles as preventative maintenance. Specialist timing chain replacement at £1,200-£1,800 resolves the issue if done promptly. If the chain has already slipped, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 Mercedes CLS 220/250 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: Injector Seal Failure ("Black Death") - The Classic Mercedes Diesel Issue
problems.rootCause: Injector seals fail, allowing unburnt diesel fuel and exhaust gases to escape past the seal. This creates a hard, tar-like carbon buildup around the injector seats - a condition commonly referred to as "Black Death". Symptoms include a chuffing or ticking noise from the engine bay, visible black residue around injectors, fuel odour, rough idling, and in severe cases, a Check Engine light.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injectors, clean bores, replace seals and copper washers
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-150k miles; effective if caught before seat damage

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - Injector Seat Re-cutting & Seal Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Re-cut injector seats, replace seals and clamp bolts with upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if seat damage has occurred; prevents recurrence

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt OM651 engine with new injectors, seals, and timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if Black Death has caused cylinder head damage or injector seizure

problems.recommendation: Injector seal failure is a common issue on Mercedes diesel engines. Don't ignore the tell-tale chuffing noise or black residue. Specialist injector seal replacement at £300-£500 is cost-effective and resolves the issue. However, if the engine has been run with leaking seals for an extended period, cylinder head damage may have occurred - in which case a rebuilt engine with new injectors and upgraded seals is the safer option.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM651 injector seal replacement for your Mercedes CLS 220/250 CDI

problems.h4: EGR Valve & Swirl Flap Failure - Loss of Power and Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: The EGR valve becomes clogged with soot and carbon deposits, leading to rough idle, check engine light, and reduced performance. Simultaneously, the plastic swirl flaps in the intake manifold can become stiff or break, with fragments sometimes entering cylinders. Common problems on the OM651 include DPF pressure sensors, exhaust temp sensors, snapped inlet manifold bolts, split turbo hoses and jammed EGRs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve and inlet ports
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; regular maintenance item

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace complete intake manifold with swirl flap assembly
repairOptions.longevity: Restores power and prevents flap fragments entering engine

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with new intake manifold and EGR components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if swirl flap fragments have damaged cylinders

problems.recommendation: Loss of power and rough idle are classic signs of EGR or swirl flap issues. Start with a diagnostic to identify the specific fault. EGR cleaning at £150-£300 is a low-cost fix if caught early. If the swirl flaps have failed, a replacement intake manifold at £550-£850 is required. Catch it early - flap debris in the cylinders can cause catastrophic engine damage.
